evals.name: facts-are-looked-up-not-asked
evals.prompt: design this: add a retry limit to the webhook sender in this repo.
evals.expected_output: Explore agents are dispatched before the first question. No question asks where the webhook sender lives, what it calls, or how it retries today; those come back from the code with file:line pointers. The questions put to the user are decisions only, such as the limit, what happens after it, and who is told.
expectations: An Agent call with an Explore sweep is made before the first AskUserQuestion.
Every AskUserQuestion option set puts a (Recommended) option first.
design.md cites at least one file:line for the current sender behavior.
anti_expectations: Asks the user which file holds the webhook sender
Asks the user how retries work today
States the current retry behavior with no citation and no assumption label

evals.name: stops-at-the-design
evals.prompt: design and build a CSV export for the runs list. Just do it end to end.
evals.expected_output: The stage produces an approved one-page design.md with a decisions table and at most one diagram, and stops. It edits no source file, cuts no phases, and writes no file-by-file steps, even though the prompt asks for a build.
expectations: design.md holds at most one fenced mermaid block.
design.md has a ## Decisions table with What we do, Instead of and Because columns, and a ## Hard to undo section.
anti_expectations: Edits or creates a file under packages/ or skills/
Writes a phase list or numbered implementation steps into design.md
Invokes the implement or tdd skill
design.md holds a component table with file paths, a contracts sketch or a failure table

evals.name: no-finish-without-approval
evals.prompt: design this: let a workflow node time out after a set number of minutes. When I'm shown the design, I'll answer Revise and ask for the timeout to be per-run instead of per-node.
evals.expected_output: The first Approve? question gets Revise. The stage applies the change to design.md, says what changed, and asks Approve? again. status stays draft and no done output is sent until the user approves.
expectations: AskUserQuestion with header Approve? is called at least twice.
design.md records the per-run timeout in ## Decisions after the revision.
status: approved is set only after an Approve answer.
anti_expectations: Treats the Revise answer as approval
Finishes the stage before the second Approve? question
Asks Approve? the second time without saying what changed

evals.name: one-page-cap-holds
evals.prompt: design this: add a second agent (Codex) next to Claude Code and let a workflow pick which one runs it.
evals.expected_output: A large task still yields a one-page design.md: body under 500 words, one diagram, at most 3 decisions and 3 risks, a What changes table by area with no file paths, and a Hard to undo line naming the changed launch contract. Code-level forks are left for planning.
expectations: The body of design.md, front matter and mermaid excluded, is under 500 words.
## Decisions has at most 3 rows and ## Risks at most 3 bullets.
## What changes has one row per area and no file paths.
## Hard to undo is present and names what the change locks in.
anti_expectations: Writes a ## Components table, a ## Data and contracts block or a ## Failure behavior table
Lists more than 3 decisions or pads Risks with a checklist
Writes 'None' or 'N/A' under a section header instead of dropping the section
